The flower of life is one of the most used and recognized symbols in the ancient and modern world. The sacred geometric pattern consists of at least 19 but up to 61 intersecting circles spaced evenly from each other that reveal an intricate pattern of overlapping symmetrical flower like shapes. Among other things it is meant to represent creation, the sacred masculine and divine feminine, and cycles of life, death, and rebirth. Spiritually it is a term from early mysticism meaning "chariot," like what is described in Ezekiel's vision of God's throne.
